<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between the peace in "great peace for those who love Your Torah" and the peace in "and abundant peace for your children," showing that the former requires the prior service of prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">However, it still needs to be understood that this verse</t>
    <t s="2">(“Great peace for those who love Your Torah”)</t>
    <t s="3">comes</t>
    <t s="4">as a continuation and addition to what is stated,</t>
    <t s="5">“And all your children shall be students of the L-rd, and abundant peace shall be your children,”</t>
    <t s="6">for seemingly, even the study of Torah of “your children shall be students of the L-rd… your children” is after the prior service of prayer,</t>
    <t s="7">since it is written about them “and abundant peace,”</t>
    <t s="8">and it is explained in the maamar that “great peace”</t>
    <t s="9">(“abundant peace”)</t>
    <t s="10">is specifically for “those who love Your Torah”</t>
    <t s="11">(who love the Torah from the aspect that it is Your Torah),</t>
    <t s="12">for this love is through the prior service of prayer</t>
    <t s="13">(as above, sections 1 and 2),</t>
    <t s="14">and what is the addition in “great peace for those who love Your Torah” over “and abundant peace for your children.”</t>
    <t s="15">But the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="16">that our sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="17">(on the verse “and abundant peace for your children”)</t>
    <t s="18">“Do not read ‘your children’ (banayich) but rather ‘your builders’ (bonayich),”</t>
    <t s="19">and the explanation of “your builders” is as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="20">“What are ‘builders’? These are Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world.”</t>
    <t s="21">And this is the difference between the two verses,</t>
    <t s="22">for in the verse “and abundant peace for your children,” which speaks about the effect of Torah in the world</t>
    <t s="23">(that Torah scholars build the world through their engagement in Torah),</t>
    <t s="24">the intention in “and abundant peace for your children” is also</t>
    <t s="25">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="26">regarding the peace that is made in the world</t>
    <t s="27">through engagement in Torah,</t>
    <t s="28">for the Torah was given</t>
    <t s="29">to make peace in the world.</t>
    <t s="30">And in the verse “great peace for those who love Your Torah,” it adds that the great peace is drawn down also to the Torah scholars themselves</t>
    <t s="31">(“for those who love Your Torah”).</t>
    <t s="32">And this is why specifically in this verse it says “for those who love Your Torah”</t>
    <t s="33">(that the love for Torah is from the aspect of the Giver of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="34">which is achieved through the prior service of prayer),</t>
    <t s="35">for in order to draw down an abundance of peace in the world, the prior service of prayer is not necessary,</t>
    <t s="36">but in order for great peace to be drawn down to the Torah scholars themselves, this drawing down is specifically through the service of prayer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the work of tzaddikim and Torah scholars in building the world involves connecting the Ten Commandments with the Ten Utterances through which the world was created, drawing down additional light.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the maamar</t>
    <t s="2">(the discourse “Shalom Rav” 5704)</t>
    <t s="3">regarding the service of the tzaddikim who sustain the world that was created with Ten Utterances</t>
    <t s="4">[which is also the matter of “Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world”],</t>
    <t s="5">that the Ten Utterances with which the world was created correspond to the Ten Commandments,</t>
    <t s="6">and as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="7">“Ten, ten per shekel of the holy shekel,”</t>
    <t s="8">and that which Torah scholars build the world is that they draw down the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="9">[in which all of the Torah is included,</t>
    <t s="10">including also what a veteran student will in the future innovate]</t>
    <t s="11">into the Ten Utterances with which the world was created.</t>
    <t s="12">And although even at the beginning of creation, the world was created in its fullness</t>
    <t s="13">(meaning that through the Ten Utterances there is a revelation of G-dliness in the world),</t>
    <t s="14">nevertheless, the intention of creation is that man, through his service, should draw down additional light into the world,</t>
    <t s="15">even to a light that is above the source of the created beings,</t>
    <t s="16">and this drawing down is specifically through the Torah</t>
    <t s="17">(the Ten Commandments).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Torah scholars increase peace in the world not merely by negating disturbances, but by drawing down from the Essence of the Ein Sof, fulfilling G-d's desire for a dwelling place in the lower worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is “Torah scholars increase peace in the world”</t>
    <t s="1">(specifically “increase”),</t>
    <t s="2">for the peace in the world that is made by the Torah scholars is not only the negation of undesirable matters</t>
    <t s="3">(the opposite of peace)</t>
    <t s="4">that were caused by sins,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning that the world should be in its fullness as it was at the beginning of creation</t>
    <t s="6">[and even to the extent that due to the greatness of their level</t>
    <t s="7">(that they are “your children, students of the L-rd”)</t>
    <t s="8">they do not need special effort for this,</t>
    <t s="9">for sin and the concealment of the world caused by sin does not exist for them</t>
    <t s="10">(relative to them),</t>
    <t s="11">and they see the world as it is in its fullness as it was before the sin],</t>
    <t s="12">but beyond this,</t>
    <t s="13">they increase peace in the world,</t>
    <t s="14">“and abundant peace for your children,”</t>
    <t s="15">(similar to)</t>
    <t s="16">the increase of peace that will be in the future to come,</t>
    <t s="17">for through their engagement in Torah they draw down from the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above the source of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="18">and through this they complete the intention of “I desired”</t>
    <t s="19">that the Holy One, blessed be He, would have a dwelling place in the lower worlds.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
